title: 30 × to Remember 0.9.0: the end of the loop
message: 30 × to Remember now has an ending. After the four milestone bosses, fate sends two reflections after you: the Hollow Champion, the you that died that day, and then the Last Rememberer, who knows every loop you've lived. Beat him to free Bleakthorpe, then take on New Game+.

items: The Hollow Champion copies your build and your moves, and counters anything you repeat
The Last Rememberer turns your whole history against you
An ending, credits, and New Game+ with tougher enemies
Two new Legendaries: the Champion's Soul and the Final Memory

title: 30 × to Remember 0.8.0: the milestone bosses
message: From loop 5, a door that shouldn't be there appears once you've survived 20 minutes. Behind it waits the Forgotten King. Beat him to go deeper, and the Clockwork Sovereign, the Maw Beneath and the Paradox Regent follow. Each one fights differently, and each drops Legendary gear that binds to your hero for good.

items: Four milestone bosses at loops 5, 10, 15 and 20, each with its own tricks
Beat each boss to go deeper: until it falls, newer creatures stay away
New Legendary gear: the King's Signet, Sovereign Gear, Abyssal Heart and Paradox Crown

title: 30 × to Remember 0.7.9: one street, three times
message: Battles now play out on hand-painted scenes of the same Bleakthorpe street, as it was, as it is, and as it will be. Look closely at the past and present: the differences are small, but they're there. The future isn't subtle at all.

items: New painted battle scenes for the past, present and future
Glowing lamps and windows, and fireflies over the ruins of the future
Distant Echo rooms and the Chapel take you back to the past

title: 30 × to Remember 0.7.8: welcome to Bleakthorpe
message: The village finally wears its name: the hamlet screen is now Bleakthorpe. The full painting is back too, with the forest and the road south lit by fireflies.

items: The hamlet is now called Bleakthorpe on screen
The full village painting is back, with the southern forest and road

title: 30 × to Remember 0.7.7: a guided tour of the hamlet
message: New to Bleakthorpe? A quick tour now shows you around the hamlet the first time you arrive, pointing out every building and button. The hamlet screen is now just the map. You can replay the tour from Settings.

items: First-visit tour of the hamlet, highlighting each place and button
Replay the tour any time from Settings
Cleaner hamlet screen: credits moved into Settings

title: 30 × to Remember 0.7.6: a cleaner hamlet
message: The hamlet screen is all map now. Menu, Party, Skills and the Dungeon are round buttons along the edges, and small gold sparkles mark each place. Press and hold the map to see every place name. Tap Party to see your team's levels and stats.

items: Round buttons on the map edges for Menu, Party, Skills and the Dungeon
Gold sparkles replace the place name tags. Press and hold the map to see the names
New Party panel shows each member's portrait, level, stats and XP

title: 30 × to Remember 0.7.5: a new hamlet
message: The hamlet has a whole new look, hand-painted, and it's alive now: the rift swirls, embers drift up from the campfire, smoke curls from the chimneys and fireflies wander the trees. Keep an eye on it. Every so often, time stutters. If you're still on an old version, tap "Get the latest version" on the main menu.

items: 0.7.3: difficulty and class balance pass
0.7.4: new rare gear suffix "of Renewal" heals a little each turn
0.7.5: new painted hamlet map with animated effects
0.7.5: every so often the hamlet freezes for a moment as the loop hiccups

title: 30 × to Remember 0.7.2: the Nemesis, new portraits and a new-look hero
message: The creature that kills a companion now keeps their true name. Bring them back as a stranger, help them remember, and a red Nemesis door will appear. Beat what's behind it to give them their name back. Lose three times and it gives the name back cursed. If you're still on an old version, tap "Get the latest version" on the main menu.

items: 0.7: Nemesis doors: the creature that killed a companion waits where they fell, and holds their true name
0.7: win to restore every stranger it holds; lose three times and they come back Unworthy, weakened forever
0.7: a full party wipe leaves one creature holding every lost name
0.7.1: new detailed portraits for every character who speaks
0.7.2: the hero fights with new painted sprites, and the wizard now waits outside his tower on the hamlet map

title: 30 × to Remember 0.6.6: a new look, inside and out
message: The whole game has been redrawn in detailed, lamplit pixel art: the hamlet, the dungeon rooms, the battle backdrops, and now every class and creature, with twice the detail they had before. The wizard, the tavern keeper, the shopkeeper and every companion you hire also talk from their own portrait. If you're still on an old version, tap "Get the latest version" on the main menu.

items: 0.6.6: every class and creature redrawn with twice the detail, shading and outlines
0.6.5: new lit battle backdrops for every room: moonlit streets in the present, overgrown ruins in the future, ghostly blue in Distant Echoes
0.6.4: dungeon rooms redrawn as torch-lit pixel-art chambers with real doors, era floors and a centrepiece for each place
0.6.3: the hamlet map redrawn at night in detailed pixel art, with frozen chimney smoke, fountain spray and a floating apple
0.6.2: the shopkeeper gets a talking portrait too
0.6.1: talking pixel-art portraits for the wizard, the tavern keeper and all eight companion classes
0.6.1: portraits for the hero, speaking enemies and the final bosses are ready for the story

title: 30 × to Remember 0.6: the bestiary arrives
message: Six updates since 30 × to Remember landed on the workbench, and the latest fills the dungeon with new creatures. Every one of them has its own trick, and the tougher ones only turn up as the loops go on. If you're still on an old version, tap "Get the latest version" on the main menu.

items: 0.6: 16 new creatures across six families, each with its own trick: charging boars, poisonous spiders, mites that steal seconds off your clock, and more
0.6: Elite rooms now roll Elite, Champion or Dread enemies with modifiers like Brutal, Volatile and Chrono-Locked
0.5: the hero's skill tree, a spider's web of six disciplines with 60 nodes and 6 hybrid keystones
0.4: gold that carries between loops, a General Store, selling, binding gear and the Wizard's Sanctum
0.3: the Cleric reworked with a Lily gauge, and healing that grows with your gear
0.2: dice rolls replaced with Diablo-style stats: armour, crits and dodge

title: New on the workbench: 30 × to Remember
message: There's a new page on the hub for games that are still being built, and the first one is 30 × to Remember. A wizard's spell went wrong and left Aetherfall stuck in time. You remember every loop. Nobody else does. It's an early build, so things will change, but it's fully playable and every review goes straight to me.

items: Every action costs time, and beating enemies wins it back
The loop always resets: your levels stay, and only soulbound gear survives
Pixel-art battles with one sprite per class, coloured for each companion
Lose a companion and they might come back as a stranger who doesn't remember you

title: New game: Python Quest!
message: Part three of the Python trilogy is here. Python Kitchen teaches you to write code, Garage Code teaches you to fix it, and Python Quest teaches you to build something real with it. A half-finished JRPG is stuck in an old cartridge, and every quest builds one piece of it. Finish all 20 and the game you built becomes Ember Crown, a mini JRPG you can play, running on your own code.

items: 20 quests in four acts: the party, the battle system, loot and saves, and the dungeon
Classes, inheritance, custom exceptions, testing, json saves and recursion
Retro pixel art, and Bit the cartridge fairy explaining every error
Bonus: Ember Crown, a mini JRPG powered by the code you wrote

title: Garage Code 2.0: the sequel to Python Kitchen
message: Garage Code has been rebuilt as the next step after Python Kitchen. In the kitchen you learn to write Python. In the garage you learn to fix it. Every car rolls in with a broken program, and Les wants it signed off. It now runs real Python 3, so you learn to read the same error messages real programmers see.

items: 20 brand-new jobs across four bays, all about finding and fixing bugs
Bugs that crash and bugs that don't: off-by-one, runaway loops, the 'or' trap and more
New ideas Kitchen doesn't cover: sorting, sets, list comprehensions, classes and files
A three-fault boss job on MOT day

title: Peekaboo Meadow: the big update
message: Peekaboo Meadow has grown. There's a softer new look, two new places to visit with ten new animals, a colouring room, and a gentle bedtime wind-down: the sun sets, the moon comes out and every animal says goodnight before falling asleep. Lovely for the last game before bed.

items: New places: the farm and the beach, each with five animals to find
Colouring: eight pictures and twelve colours
Bedtime wind-down: tap the moon, or set a timer in the grown-ups menu
A softer, gentler look with the same bold colours

title: Solaris Gambit Update 5: Earth & Wind
message: The last two elements are here. Gorran Deepdelve has lived inside the same mountain for forty years, and sky-pirate Kestrel Vane has spent most of them raiding it. Beat the Hexbound Stranger to meet them, then collect all 15 cards to raise the Skyroot Colossus. We've also made saves safer and moved the Gauntlet to unlock after all eight rivals.

items: Two new rivals: Gorran Deepdelve and Kestrel Vane
15 new Earth & Wind cards and their own pack in the shop
Skyroot Colossus legend and Stone and Sky achievement
Safer saves: a backup copy restores your progress if it goes missing
Chapter legends stay a mystery until you beat both rivals

title: Solaris Gambit Update 4: Water & Thunder
message: The third chapter rolls in off the coast. Vael Stormcrow whips up the storms and Mother Nerissa has spent thirty years calming the seas he churns. Beat Lady Corvina to meet them, then collect all 15 cards to raise the Maelstrom Leviathan.

items: Two new rivals: Vael Stormcrow and Mother Nerissa
15 new Water & Thunder cards and their own pack in the shop
Maelstrom Leviathan legend for completing the set
Calm and Storm achievement

title: Solaris Gambit Update 3: Shadow & Holy
message: A new chapter about two old allies turned enemies. Sir Caedric the Fallen broke his oath to the cathedral, and Oracle Seraphine has never forgiven him. Beat Sel & Nara to unlock it, and collect all 15 cards to earn the Eclipse Seraph.

items: Two new rivals: Sir Caedric the Fallen and Oracle Seraphine
15 new Shadow & Holy cards and their own pack in the shop
Eclipse Seraph legend for completing the set
Light and Shade achievement, and chapter cards in Gauntlet drafts

title: Python Kitchen 2.2: your pass, your specials
message: The pass now fills up as you learn: every ticket you clear adds a piece of kit, from a chopping board to pots, pans and a service bell, until it's a proper busy working pass. There's a recipe binder with a short page on every new idea, and graduates can write their own tickets and send them to friends as Chef's specials.

items: The pass fills up with kit as you clear tickets
Recipe binder: a page on every new idea
Chef's specials: write and share your own tickets

title: Python Kitchen 2.1: graduation day
message: Python Kitchen has a proper main menu, a one-minute guided tour of your first ticket, a quick recap quiz after each service, and a brand-new graduation project: build a working till that takes orders, catches bad input and prints a receipt. Clear it to become Chef Patron.

items: Main menu with settings, reviews, Ko-fi and install
Guided first ticket for brand-new coders
Recap quizzes after every service
Graduation project: ticket 25, The Pass Is Yours
Chef's voice is now off by default

title: Fairway Tales: play with friends online
message: You can now play Fairway Tales with your friends, each on your own phone, wherever you are. Make a room, send the code, and up to four of you play the same nine holes with the same pins and the same wind. Scores update live between holes, and a little pop-up tells you when a friend makes a birdie.

items: Play with friends online: rooms for up to 4 players with live scores
Fixed a rare freeze that could lock the game after a short backspin shot
Skyreach best rounds now appear on the online leaderboard

title: Fairway Tales 1.0: the story is complete!
message: Fairway Tales has reached version 1.0. Chapter 5 takes you to Skyreach for the Tour Championship: a clifftop course above the clouds, with chasms to carry and the world number one waiting in the final. Win it and the story gets a proper ending.

items: Chapter 5: Skyreach, with 9 new holes, 4 new rivals and 4 new epic clubs
Club rework: every club starts at 10, and rarity and level boost your fitted parts
Pick your ball: Distance, Tour, Soft or Heavy
Friendlier first few minutes, with tips on your first shots and a quick-start guide

title: New for kids: Peekaboo Meadow!
message: Our first game for little ones is here. A sunny meadow where everything does something when you tap it: animals pop out of the bushes, the sun giggles and clouds rain flowers. A friendly voice asks your little one to find each animal, so no reading is needed and nobody ever loses.

items: Find the bunny, hedgehog, fox, frog and bird to fill the star jar
Balloon party every five stars
Press-and-hold grown-ups settings for sounds, voice and the find-it game

title: New game: Garage Code!
message: Game number six is the second learn-to-code game, this time set in a car garage. Les the foreman hands you jobs, you write Python to sign them off, and the car on the ramp reacts to every line you write. No experience needed.

items: 10 jobs from print() to functions, with a short manual page for each new idea
Tyre checks, fault codes and a boss-level MOT day tested on hidden cars
Make your own jobs and share them with a mate

title: New game: Python Kitchen!
message: Game number five is a bit different: it teaches you to code. Chef Dorran calls the orders from the pass, you write real Python to clear each ticket, and you work your way up from Kitchen Porter to Head Chef. No experience needed.

items: 24 tickets across breakfast, lunch, dinner and late service
Practice station and a full Python cookbook with runnable examples
Installs to your home screen and plays offline

title: New game: Metropolitan Misadventure!
message: Game number four is here. A slapstick open-world crime caper where you nick cars, run dodgy jobs for five district contacts and build a criminal empire. Free to play and installable like the others.

items: Five districts, each with its own contact and story chain
Jobs, safe houses, businesses and a casino
Installs to your home screen and plays offline

title: Introducing the public leaderboards!
message: Both games now have online leaderboards, so you can see how you stack up against everyone else.

items: New public leaderboard: who caught what
Catches show fish size and star rating
New daily challenge leaderboard
Best round on each course
Holes-in-one hall of fame
